title: Same Output. Different Evaluators. Different Verdicts.

intro.before: Every prompt or model change needs a verdict. The evaluator you pick decides

bullets.text: Checks the output equals the reference
Free, instant and fully reproducible
Ideal for labels, numbers and JSON fields
Fails correct answers worded differently
Scores shared words and phrases vs a reference
Standard for translation and summaries
Deterministic and easy to track over time
Misses paraphrases; rewards surface matches
Compares meaning with embeddings (BERTScore)
Credits paraphrases that n-grams miss
Cheap once the model is loaded
Similar text can still be wrong (negation)
Grades against a rubric and explains why
Handles open-ended answers at scale
Can check faithfulness to given context
Biased by position, length, self-preference
Judge picks the better of two answers
Often more consistent than absolute scores
Win rates feed Elo-style leaderboards
Relative only: A beats B, not A is good
Captures nuance, tone and domain correctness
Ground truth for calibrating LLM judges
Catches failures no metric was built for
Slow and costly; reviewers disagree

principles.sub: Exact match and schema checks first; LLM judges for open-ended quality.
Grade a sample by hand and check agreement before trusting automated scores.
Evals on real, messy inputs catch what synthetic benchmarks miss.

rows.q: Translation or summary vs a gold
High stakes or a new domain

quote.big: An eval you trust beats ten you don't.
quote.small: Measure the failure you actually fear.
